title: Aurora: Continuous Workload Profiler and Heuristic Batching Custodian (pilot)
creator: Renee Caldwell
description: Build a pilot 'Aurora' service that continuously profiles request-level workload signatures and recommends conservative batching and caching parameter tweaks. Goals: reduce per-token serving cost without violating latency SLOs; produce human-reviewable proposals; enable safe apply (shadow/canary) and automated rollback on regressions. The engine must combine short-term telemetry (1m windows) with longer-term workload fingerprints (24h) and surface per-route policies plus global heuristics for KV-cache eligibility, batch size, batching-window-ms, and preferred execution backend. Deliverables: profiler pipeline, heuristic engine, proposal diff UI payload, safe-apply automation, and rollout runbook.
acceptance_criteria: Profiler ingests sampled traces and produces per-route signature histograms within 5% accuracy versus ground truth
Heuristic engine outputs proposals with expected cost delta and estimated latency impact for 95% of active routes
Safe-apply workflow implements shadow-apply and canary with automated rollback if latency p95 increases > 8% or error-rate increases >0.5% absolute
Pilot achieves >=6% net token-cost reduction on curated test tenants without breaching latency SLOs
tasks: Instrument request sampling: add deterministic fingerprinting for prompt length, kv-hit-rate estimate, model variant, and client priority
Build hourly aggregation job to compute route-level distributions and novelty detector
Implement heuristics module: conservative defaults, cost-quality objective function, and decay windows
Design proposal schema and 'diff' payload for Console review (per-route + global summary)
Wire safe-apply: shadow-apply -> canary -> gradual rollout with rollback triggers
Add dashboard panels (Grafana) and alert rules for rollback conditions
End-to-end integration test and run pilot on two internal tenants
decisions: Use blended objective: cost_per_1000_tokens + lambda * latency_p95 where lambda tuned during pilot
Conservative first-pass: cap batch-size increase to +30% and batching-window to +50ms for canary
KV-cache proposals only where route-level estimated KV-hit > 20% to avoid negative cache churn
All proposals must be human-reviewable with a single-click approve/abort in Console before non-shadow apply
telemetry_findings: Initial sampling (48h) shows a bimodal prompt-length distribution on search routes: 75% short (<64 tokens), 25% long (>512 tokens)
KV estimates correlate strongly with prompt prefix repeats on assistant-like routes; estimated kv-hit median 28%
Microburst patterns observed: 2-3s spikes where small batches (1-3) dominate; naive batching-window increases there cause P95 latency regressions
Simulated conservative proposals show median cost delta -8.2% and P95 latency delta +3.1% on internal dataset
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (shadow-only): 2 weeks, compare cost/latency signals in shadow against control, no production apply
Phase 1 (canary): 48h per route with traffic slice 2-5%, automated rollback if thresholds breached
Phase 2 (gradual expand): stepwise increases (5% -> 20% -> 50%) with monitoring gates and manual gating option
Rollback strategy: immediate revert and create postmortem if any canary shows >8% P95 regression or >0.5% absolute error-rate increase
